{{short description|Norwegian mathematician (1905–1973)}}
{{Use dmy dates | date=January 2025}}
[[File:WilhelmLjunggren.png|thumb|Wilhelm Ljunggren]]
'''Wilhelm Ljunggren''' (7 October 1905 – 25 January 1973) was a [[Norwegian people|Norwegian]] [[mathematician]], specializing in [[number theory]].<ref name="mactutor">{{MacTutor|id=Ljunggren|title=Wilhelm Ljunggren}}.</ref>

==Career==
Ljunggren was born in [[Oslo|Kristiania]] and [[examen artium|finished]] his secondary education in 1925. He studied at the [[University of Oslo]], earning a [[cand.real.|master's degree]] in 1931 under the supervision of [[Thoralf Skolem]], and found employment as a secondary school mathematics teacher in [[Bergen]], following Skolem who had moved in 1930 to the Chr. Michelsen Institute there. While in Bergen, Ljunggren continued his studies, earning a [[dr.philos.]] from the University of Oslo in 1937.<ref name="mactutor"/><ref name=hvem>{{cite encyclopedia|year=1973|title=Ljunggren, Wilhelm|encyclopedia=[[Hvem er hvem?]]|editor=Steenstrup, Bjørn|publisher=Aschehoug|location=Oslo|url=https://runeberg.org/hvemerhvem/1973/0346.html|page=346|language=Norwegian|access-date=25 April 2014}}</ref>

In 1938 he moved to work as a teacher at Hegdehaugen in Oslo. In 1943 he became a fellow of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]], and he also joined the [[Selskapet til Vitenskapenes Fremme]]. He was appointed as a [[docent]] at the University of Oslo in 1948, but in 1949 he returned to Bergen as a professor at the recently founded [[University of Bergen]]. He moved back to the University of Oslo again in 1956, where he served until his death in 1973 in Oslo.<ref name="mactutor"/><ref name=hvem/><ref name=snl>{{cite encyclopedia|year=|title=Wilhelm Ljunggren|encyclopedia=[[Store norske leksikon]]|editor=|publisher=|location=|url=http://www.snl.no/Wilhelm_Ljunggren|language=Norwegian|access-date=25 April 2014}}</ref>

===Research===
Ljunggren's research concerned number theory, and in particular [[Diophantine equation]]s.<ref name="mactutor"/> He showed that [[Stella octangula number|Ljunggren's equation]],
:''X''<sup>2</sup>&nbsp;=&nbsp;2''Y''<sup>4</sup>&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1.
has only the two integer solutions (1,1) and (239,13);<ref>{{citation
 | last = Ljunggren | first = Wilhelm
 | issue = 5
 | journal = Avh. Norske Vid. Akad. Oslo. I.
 | mr = 0016375
 | page = 27
 | title = Zur Theorie der Gleichung ''x''<sup>2</sup>&nbsp;+&nbsp;1&nbsp;=&nbsp;''Dy''<sup>4</sup>
 | volume = 1942
 | year = 1942}}.</ref> however, his proof was complicated, and after [[Louis J. Mordell]] conjectured that it could be simplified, simpler proofs were published by several other authors.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Steiner | first1 = Ray
 | last2 = Tzanakis | first2 = Nikos
 | doi = 10.1016/S0022-314X(05)80029-0
 | issue = 2
 | journal = Journal of Number Theory
 | mr = 1092598
 | pages = 123–132
 | title = Simplifying the solution of Ljunggren's equation ''X''<sup>2</sup>&nbsp;+&nbsp;1&nbsp;=&nbsp;2''Y''<sup>4</sup>
 | url = http://www.math.uoc.gr/~tzanakis/Papers/LjunggrenEq.pdf
 | volume = 37
 | year = 1991| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last = Draziotis | first = Konstantinos A.
 | doi = 10.4064/cm109-1-2
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Colloquium Mathematicum
 | mr = 2308822
 | pages = 9–11
 | title = The Ljunggren equation revisited
 | volume = 109
 | year = 2007| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref><ref>{{citation|last=Siksek|first=Samir|title=Descents on Curves of Genus I|url=http://www.warwick.ac.uk/~masgaj/theses/siksek_thesis.pdf|pages=16–17|year=1995|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809101031/http://homepages.warwick.ac.uk/~masgaj/theses/siksek_thesis.pdf|series=Ph.D. thesis|publisher=University of Exeter|archive-date=9 August 2017}}.</ref>

Ljunggren also posed the question of finding the integer solutions to the [[Ramanujan–Nagell equation]]
:2<sup>''n''</sup> &minus; 7 = ''x''<sup>2</sup>
(or equivalently, of finding [[triangular number|triangular]] [[Mersenne number]]s) in 1943,<ref>{{citation | first=Wilhelm|last=Ljunggren | title=Oppgave nr 2 | journal=Norsk Mat. Tidsskr. | volume=25 | year=1943 | pages=29 }}.</ref> independently of [[Srinivasa Ramanujan]] who had asked the same question in 1913.

Ljunggren's publications are collected in a book edited by [[Paulo Ribenboim]].<ref>{{citation|title=Collected papers of Wilhelm Ljunggren|editor-first=Paulo|editor-last=Ribenboim|editor-link=Paulo Ribenboim|publisher=Queen's University|location=Kingston, Ontario|series=Queen's papers in pure and applied mathematics|volume=115|year=2003|isbn=0-88911-836-1}}.</ref>
